0.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table S1901 — median household income by census tract
0.note: On disk. The libraries case reads the same file. Only the census-tract layer carries a true median; NTA and community district carry a population-weighted mean of tract medians.

1.name: NYPD complaints, 2026 Q1, pulled 2026-06-29
1.note: 133,114 complaints, every one geocoded. Severity weights felony 3, misdemeanor 2, violation 1, the same as scripts/pairwise_socioeconomic_regression.py. Crime is point data, so a count and an area aggregate exactly. Thus every layer gets a true value, unlike the income proxy. WARNING: the file name says year to date, but the record stops on 2026-03-31. 94.8% of the complaints fall in January to March 2026, and the rest are late reports of older events. Read this source as 1 winter quarter, never as a full year.

2.name: ACS 5-Year 2024, table B01003 — total population by census tract
2.note: Weights the income aggregation, and supplies the denominator of the per-capita crime rate. A sum aggregates exactly, so the population of a polygon needs no approximation.

3.name: NYPD Complaint Data Historic — transit premise only
3.where: prem_typ_desc='TRANSIT - NYC SUBWAY' AND cmplnt_fr_dt >= '2024-01-01' AND cmplnt_fr_dt < '2026-07-01'
3.note: 59,555 complaints inside the subway system. This table stops on 2025-12-31, thus source 4 carries the rest of the window. The premise filter runs on the server. The record puts each complaint at its station, and it also names the station in `station_name`.

4.name: NYPD Complaint Data Current (Year To Date) — transit premise only
4.where: prem_typ_desc='TRANSIT - NYC SUBWAY' AND cmplnt_fr_dt >= '2024-01-01' AND cmplnt_fr_dt < '2026-07-01'
4.note: 17,174 complaints. Sources 3 and 4 together give 76,729 rows, and no complaint number repeats. The 2026Q1 file of source 1 holds 8,903 transit rows, which is too thin to grade a station.

5.name: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership: 2020-2024
5.note: 120,855,567 rows. The pull sums `ridership` on the SERVER and groups by `station_complex_id`, thus the network carries 428 rows. This is the exposure of the crime rate.

6.name: MTA Subway Hourly Ridership: Beginning 2025
6.note: The MTA cuts the hourly record at the end of 2024, thus sources 5 and 6 together cover the crime window. 428 complexes report, and the 19 Staten Island Railway complexes do not.

7.name: MTA Subway Stations
7.note: 496 stations. The table maps `station_id` to `complex_id` and gives each station its GTFS point, thus it is both the roll-up table and the target of the complaint join. `entrances.parquet` carries the same 2 ids, so the join needs no name match.
